biggestGap: The board is lit as a self-luminous plane instead of a reflective one: the ~20 flames sitting directly on the kerb put no contact pool, no reflected streak and no falloff onto the marble, so the light squares hold one near-uniform blown value from the near kerb to the far rank while every flame reads as a sprite pasted over a lightbox. Drive the board's brightness from the flames themselves — hot grazing pools within a metre or two of each flame, blurred vertical reflections of flames and plinths in the polished stone, and a real luminance gradient down the long axis — and let the dark squares hold deep navy between them.
critiqueDetail: I picked the film (panel B) instantly and with high confidence; the render is not close. Round 3's inversion has been over-corrected rather than fixed. The board is now the bright object, which is right, but it is bright the way a backlit panel is bright, not the way polished marble in a dark room is bright. Its light squares sit at one flat near-white value across the entire length of the board — same at the near kerb as at the far rank eight metres away — and there is not a single flame reflection, contact pool or grazing specular sweep anywhere on the surface, even though a dozen flames are burning on the kerb inches from it. fracBlown is 2.3x the reference (0.01479 vs 0.00649) and essentially all of that excess is on that one plane. In the film the marble's value is entirely a consequence of what is reflecting in it: pale pools near the flames, a broad soft specular bloom across the mid-field, blurred inverted flame streaks, and the far end falling away — the checker pattern stays legible because the dark navy squares hold their value while the light ones vary. Ours reads as two constant tones with noise on top. The tone response is also wrong in the surround: the room outside the board has collapsed to near-flat black cardboard with a hard rounded-rectangle mask at the frame edge that reads as a geometric matte, not a lens vignette; the film's corners fall off smoothly and the piers behind still carry modelled cool ambient at legible mid-tone. detailByBand is the clearest numeric fingerprint of the failure: the reference is flat across scales (0.02014 / 0.02098 / 0.02019) while ours is 0.01023 / 0.06246 / 0.04841 — half the coarse-band energy, meaning almost none of the large-scale luminance modelling that falloff and reflection produce, and three times the mid- and fine-band energy, which is the uniform salt-and-pepper stipple standing in for marble veining and for grain. detailTotal 0.04025 vs 0.02036 is 'right total, wrong places' exactly as warned. The global tonal stats remain well-matched (medianLuminance, fracShadow, fracDeepShadow, warmFraction all within 0.011) and gradientAnisotropy 1.169 vs 1.462 confirms the render lacks the directional structure the film's raking light gives it.

history.gap: Flames are self-luminous sprites that emit no light — no warm pools, no uplight, no falloff — leaving one uniform cold ambient that also lifts the blacks (fracDeepShadow 0.135 vs 0.331).

Flames now emit light but with unbounded range, and the global ambient is still too high, so nothing reaches black — the whole colonnade is evenly lit to the top of frame and fracDeepShadow fell further to 0.104 vs 0.331.

Light distribution is inverted — the rear architecture is the brightest large area while the board sits flat and dark with no cream light squares, no specular bloom and no reflections; the film lights the board and lets the room go black.

Over-corrected: the board is now a self-luminous flat panel, near-uniform and blown from near kerb to far rank (fracBlown 0.0148 vs 0.0065), with no per-flame contact pools, no flame reflections in the marble and no falloff down the long axis — so the flames read as decals on a lightbox. detailByBand [0.0102, 0.0625, 0.0484] vs [0.0201, 0.0210, 0.0202] shows half the coarse-scale luminance modelling and 3x the fine-scale stipple.
